lines.say: In 1982, seven people died in Chicago from poisoned pills.
The pills were Tie-lenol, and nobody even knew yet how far it went.
So the company pulled every bottle off every shelf. Thirty-one million bottles. Over a hundred million dollars, gone.
The tampering wasn't even their fault. Someone put the poison in after the bottles left the factory.
They ran warnings everywhere, then rebuilt the packaging with a safety seal. Damn expensive.
People expected the brand to die. Instead, customers came back, because the company had put them first.
Thirty-one million bottles, pulled before anyone forced them to.
Your clients are the same. The ones who stay are the ones you reach out to first.
